title: Functional Groups and Reactions

cards.b: Ethane is a gas; ethanol is in drinks and sanitiser; ethanoic acid is vinegar. Their carbon skeletons look similar. What changes is a small cluster of atoms called a functional group. Learn the groups and you can predict the chemistry of thousands of compounds.
A functional group is an atom or group of atoms that gives a molecule its characteristic reactions. Molecules with the same group behave alike, whatever their size.

• Alcohol (-OH): ethanol C2H5OH.
  • Aldehyde (-CHO): ethanal CH3CHO; formaldehyde.
  • Ketone (C=O in the chain): propanone (acetone) CH3COCH3.
  • Carboxylic acid (-COOH): ethanoic acid CH3COOH.
  • Ester (-COO-): fruity smells; ethyl ethanoate.
  • Amine (-NH2): methylamine; amino acids carry both -NH2 and -COOH.
  • Halide (-Cl, -Br): chloroethane.

• Addition: a double bond opens: C2H4 + H2O → C2H5OH.
  • Substitution: one atom or group replaced by another: CH4 + Cl2 → CH3Cl + HCl.
  • Elimination: a small molecule leaves, making a double bond.
  • Oxidation: alcohol becomes aldehyde or acid.

Making it: fermentation of sugars by yeast: C6H12O6 → 2C2H5OH + 2CO2. Industrial route: addition of steam to ethene.

Oxidising it: ethanol → ethanal → ethanoic acid (vinegar), by oxidising agents or bacteria.

Burning it: C2H5OH + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O.

Reacting with sodium: 2C2H5OH + 2Na → 2C2H5ONa + H2.

Esterification: acid + alcohol ⇌ ester + water, with a little sulphuric acid as catalyst.

CH3COOH + C2H5OH ⇌ CH3COOC2H5 + H2O

Esters give fruit and flower fragrance. Reverse with a strong base (hydrolysis) and you get saponification: fat + NaOH → glycerol + soap. Soaps have a long non-polar tail that grips grease and a polar head that loves water.

Ethanol, C2H6O: 2 x 12 + 6 x 1 + 16 = 46 g/mol. Fermenting 180 g glucose (180 g/mol) = 1 mol gives 2 mol ethanol = 92 g (theoretical).

Which group? CH3CH2CH2COOH has -COOH: carboxylic acid, butanoic acid. CH3COCH3 has C=O between carbons: ketone.

• Alcohols are not bases like NaOH; the -OH is not released as hydroxide.
  • Carboxylic acids are weak acids, not strong.
  • Fermentation is anaerobic; vinegar-making needs oxygen.
  • Industrial ethanol is made differently from drinking alcohol, though the compound is the same. Denatured alcohol is poisonous.

India's sugarcane molasses ferment into ethanol, used in petrol blending, sanitiser (which saw huge demand in 2020), and chemicals. India's ethanol blending programme aimed at 20 percent blending (E20), cutting crude imports and emissions. Indian pharma also leans on organic synthesis: functional-group chemistry lies behind most generic drugs made in India.

• Functional groups: -OH, -CHO, C=O, -COOH, ester, -NH2.
  • Reaction types: addition, substitution, elimination, oxidation.
  • Fermentation: C6H12O6 → 2C2H5OH + 2CO2; esterification: acid + alcohol ⇌ ester + water.

2. How do you turn ethanol into vinegar?
